scope: All 102 published Voice Path lesson previews, with lesson-specific singing protocols, explicit evidence limits, and safety stop rules.

instructionConventions.practiceTiming: Segment durations sum to catalog minutes and include setup, rests, review, and recovery. They are attention blocks, not competence deadlines or continuous-phonation requirements.
instructionConventions.comfort: Use repeatable comfortable pitches and moderate intensity. Stop for pain, burning, sudden hoarseness, loss of range, or a speaking-voice change. Persistent symptoms need a qualified clinician, not another app attempt.
instructionConventions.measurement: A missing or low-confidence reading is missing evidence, never a pass. Pitch traces, range endpoints, scores, sustain timers, ring ratio, and cycle dose retain the narrower meanings stated per lesson; ring ratio is not a strain measure.
instructionConventions.selfReport: Register, break continuity, vowel consistency, diction, articulation, dynamics, passaggio, belt safety, improvisation quality, vibrato, ornament identity, style, production weight, effects, and harmony remain human judgments where the app has no validating measurement.
instructionConventions.referenceAudio: Reference playback supplies a target, not evidence of the singer. Stop it before recording or judging microphone input.
instructionConventions.healthBoundary: These lessons teach practice decisions and stop rules. They do not diagnose, treat, medically clear, or certify freedom from strain or injury.

integrationNote.catalogInventory: The Voice catalog publishes 102 actual lesson objects across 34 modules. This resource authors those objects only; it does not invent the 135 additional lessons implied by lessonsTotal fields.
integrationNote.proofBoundary: Guided instruction changes content availability, not measurement capability. Self-assessment text states when playback or a human judgment is the only evidence.
integrationNote.loader: LessonInstructionLibrary.loadBundled must merge voice-instruction after the three guitar instruction resources.
integrationNote.reviewBoundary: A qualified vocal pedagogy and clinical-safety review remains required before presenting advanced belt, weight, range-extension, or effects guidance as professionally reviewed instruction.

lessons.title: Why Loud Playback Ruins Pitch
lessons.objective: Device volume above half bleeds into the mic and ruins pitch detection. It reads as a broken app. Work at a comfortable intensity and preserve the evidence boundary for Set Up Your Space.

steps.title: Set a safe baseline
steps.action: Silence reference playback, lower speaker volume below halfway, and use wired headphones when available. Keep the microphone opening clear and stay one relaxed hand-span away.
steps.lookCheck: Posture, room, device, and the planned stop rule are settled before the first attempt.
steps.listenCheck: Begin from an easy, repeatable sound; silence playback before judging your own voice.

steps.title: Name the target: Room setup and clean input
steps.action: Device volume above half bleeds into the mic and ruins pitch detection. It reads as a broken app. Say what will count as complete in this lesson before practising, and keep the attempt inside the range and duration you can repeat comfortably.
steps.lookCheck: The input trace starts with your voice, settles while you sing, and returns to quiet instead of moving with playback or room noise.
steps.listenCheck: Your recorded voice is clear enough to follow without echo, clipping, a second voice, or loud accompaniment.

steps.title: Hear the distinction
steps.action: Make two brief, comfortable examples of the idea in “Why Loud Playback Ruins Pitch.” Change only the named variable, record both, then return to the easier baseline. Make one comfortable sustained sound, then leave a full quiet gap before the next. Change only one room or device setting at a time so you can hear what fixed the input.
steps.lookCheck: The input trace starts with your voice, settles while you sing, and returns to quiet instead of moving with playback or room noise.
steps.listenCheck: Your recorded voice is clear enough to follow without echo, clipping, a second voice, or loud accompaniment.

steps.title: Judge only the evidence you have
steps.action: Review the take once. Keep the observation even if it is incomplete, and do not turn a missing measurement into a pass. This lesson can establish: A clean stretch of confidently voiced input under the setup used for this attempt.
steps.lookCheck: The saved result names the attempted key, pitch, tempo, or setup needed to interpret it; no missing signal is counted as success.
steps.listenCheck: Use playback and the available reading only for their stated job. They do not establish: Microphone calibration, room treatment, vocal technique, pitch accuracy, or a diagnosis of any voice problem.

mistakeRecovery.observation: The target disappears when the range, volume, speed, or duration increases.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: If the trace follows the speaker or jumps while you are silent, stop playback, lower the output, move away from noise, and try one fresh sound.

mistakeRecovery.observation: The display and your playback seem to disagree, or the app reports no confident result.
mistakeRecovery.recovery: Treat the reading as missing, not as a pass or failure. Stop reference audio, restore a quiet setup, make one easier fresh attempt, and keep the human listening judgment separate from the measurement.

lessons.title: Low First, High Second, Neither Forced
lessons.objective: Comfortable, not extreme. The number we want is the one you can use. Work at a comfortable intensity and preserve the evidence boundary for Your Range.

steps.title: Set a safe baseline
steps.action: Start near the middle of your comfortable speaking range after a gentle hum. Keep the jaw loose and choose a small lip trill, hum, or easy vowel rather than a loud call.
steps.lookCheck: Posture, room, device, and the planned stop rule are settled before the first attempt.
steps.listenCheck: Begin from an easy, repeatable sound; silence playback before judging your own voice.

steps.title: Name the target: Range scan and voice type
steps.action: Comfortable, not extreme. The number we want is the one you can use. Say what will count as complete in this lesson before practising, and keep the attempt inside the range and duration you can repeat comfortably.
steps.lookCheck: The trace moves continuously through the pitches you actually produced; an endpoint is kept only after the detector holds it confidently.
steps.listenCheck: Both slides remain conversational in effort. The last usable note sounds repeatable, not like an extreme reached once.

steps.title: Hear the distinction
steps.action: Make two brief, comfortable examples of the idea in “Low First, High Second, Neither Forced.” Change only the named variable, record both, then return to the easier baseline. Glide down only while the sound stays easy, reset, then glide up separately. Stop before squeezing, pain, scratchiness, or the urge to reach for a number.
steps.lookCheck: The trace moves continuously through the pitches you actually produced; an endpoint is kept only after the detector holds it confidently.
steps.listenCheck: Both slides remain conversational in effort. The last usable note sounds repeatable, not like an extreme reached once.

steps.title: Judge only the evidence you have
steps.action: Review the take once. Keep the observation even if it is incomplete, and do not turn a missing measurement into a pass. This lesson can establish: The comfortable low and high pitches detected in this scan and the category estimate derived from those extremes.
steps.lookCheck: The saved result names the attempted key, pitch, tempo, or setup needed to interpret it; no missing signal is counted as success.
steps.listenCheck: Use playback and the available reading only for their stated job. They do not establish: Passaggio pitches, permanent voice type, vocal health, strain, or the widest note you could force once.

mistakeRecovery.recovery: If an endpoint needs extra volume, a lifted chin, or neck effort, discard it, return to the middle, and keep the last easy repeatable note.

lessons.title: Ribs Out, Shoulders Still
lessons.objective: What to move and what to leave alone. Work at a comfortable intensity and preserve the evidence boundary for Breathe Low.

steps.title: Set a safe baseline
steps.action: Stand or sit tall without locking the ribs. Let the shoulders remain quiet while the lower ribs and abdomen respond to an unforced inhale.
steps.lookCheck: Posture, room, device, and the planned stop rule are settled before the first attempt.
steps.listenCheck: Begin from an easy, repeatable sound; silence playback before judging your own voice.

steps.title: Name the target: Low breath and rib expansion
steps.action: What to move and what to leave alone. Say what will count as complete in this lesson before practising, and keep the attempt inside the range and duration you can repeat comfortably.
steps.lookCheck: The shoulders do not rise sharply, the neck stays quiet, and the body does not fold during the final seconds.
steps.listenCheck: The hiss stays even rather than surging at the start and fading to almost nothing at the end.

steps.title: Hear the distinction
steps.action: Make two brief, comfortable examples of the idea in “Ribs Out, Shoulders Still.” Change only the named variable, record both, then return to the easier baseline. Release a narrow, even hiss. Favor steadiness over duration, and end with air still available instead of collapsing or bearing down.

lessons.title: Where Your Voice Changes Gear

steps.title: Set a safe baseline
steps.action: Warm up gently, then choose a narrow range that crosses a place where production tends to change. Use moderate volume and short attempts.
steps.lookCheck: Posture, room, device, and the planned stop rule are settled before the first attempt.

steps.action: Make two brief, comfortable examples of the idea in “Where Your Voice Changes Gear.” Change only the named variable, record both, then return to the easier baseline.
